question: What type of plate boundaries occur along spreading centres where plates are breaking apart and pushing upward from the mantle by magma to form a new crust?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Divergent boundaries.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Divergent boundaries** occur along spreading centers where plates are breaking apart and pushing upward from the mantle by magma to form a new crust.
 
• These boundaries are also known as **constructive boundaries.**
 
• It is formed by **tectonic plates pulling apart from each other.**
 
• It pushes apart two or more plates by the rise of magma from the Earth's mantle towards the surface.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Transform boundaries**

 
 
• A transform boundary is formed as tectonic** plates slide horizontally past each other but parts of these plates get stuck at the places where they touch.**
 
• These boundaries are** conservative **because plate interaction occurs **without creating or destroying crust.**
 
• They don't play any role in the birth of mountains or oceans, but sometimes they can trigger large earthquakes.
 
 
 
• **Convergent boundaries**
 
 
• A convergent plate boundary is formed **when tectonic plates crash into each other.**
 
• They are also known as **destructive boundaries.**
 
• These can **create deep trenches **and the** Himalayan Mountain Range** is the best active example of the crash of continental convergent plate boundaries.
 
• These boundaries are often **subduction zones.**
